findings.title: Principal embodiment: how the purge gap opens, and how air reaches it, is not disclosed and the stated geometry contradicts itself
findings.attack: Five gaps, each on the face of the text. (1) Direction. The purge gap lies between the outer surface of the ring and the bore around it, and is said to open when the wall moves outward. An outer surface that moves outward moves towards the bore that bounds the gap. The text never says which contact closes the gap at rest, or why an outward movement breaks that contact instead of tightening it. (2) Load path. The description does not say which surface of the seat ring the purge shoulder bears on, in which axial direction the load acts, or what reacts it. [0113] puts the load at the upper edge, which is the sealing edge that the sealing face has just left; the figure instruction puts the purge shoulder at the fit-band end, which is the end pressed into the bore and seated on the locating shoulder, where a load passes into the core body without crossing the convoluted wall. (3) Sign of the deformation. [0134], [0170] and claim 22 have the axial load flatten the convolution; [0172] says that a single outward bow, which it equates with one convolution, increases under axial load. Claim 24 claims the single outward bow in dependence on claim 22, so one claim requires the bow to flatten while the description says it grows. (4) Inlet. Only the exit of the purge flow is described. With the outer surface of the ring pressed into the bore, no route is identified by which air at pump pressure enters the gap from upstream without passing the sealing edge. (5) As built. [0202] states that the fit band, the free portion and the core body bore relief are not the tested construction, so the construction that did run for forty cycles is not described in the one respect that matters. An examiner puts this as lack of enablement of the only tested embodiment and of claims 16 to 19, 45, 58 and 65; an opponent uses the contradiction as the verifiable fact that raises serious doubt.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add disclosure taken from the inventor's prototype and drawings: the surface of the seat ring on which the purge shoulder bears and the direction of the load; the support that reacts it; the contact that closes the purge gap at rest and how the movement of the wall opens it; the entry and the exit of the purge flow; and the retention actually used in the tested valve cores. Reconcile [0134], [0170] and [0172], and claim 24 with claim 22. No claim is narrowed. If the inventor's answer is that part of the wall moves inward to open the gap, claims 1 to 3 need the genus wording 'radial deflection', which [0014] already uses.

findings.title: Example 1 cannot have been run as recorded: forty 24-hour cycles in a nine-day test
findings.attack: One inflation cycle includes a hold of 24 hours. Forty cycles need at least forty days; the eighteen, fourteen and twelve cycles of the conventional valve cores need eighteen, fourteen and twelve. The recorded test period is nine days. The leak-down figures are each stated per 24 hours, so the hold cannot simply be read out. The dates, the hold period or the cycle counts are wrong. Example 1 is the only data in the application, it is presented as an actual example in [0278], and the Background and the Technical problem rely on it at [0003] and [0012]. An examiner gives the example no weight; an opponent uses the inconsistency to discredit every effect the application asserts; in the US the accuracy of results reported as actual is a matter counsel must clear before filing.
findings.least_narrowing_action: The inventor checks the laboratory record and states which of the three is correct. The text is then corrected to the record and to nothing else. If some holds were shorter than 24 hours, say so and state how each leak-down figure per 24 hours was obtained. No value is to be adjusted without the record.

findings.title: Inventive step: the application's own inspection contradicts the effect attributed to the purge gap
findings.attack: Closest art: the conventional tyre valve core of [0003], a spring-biased poppet on a seat in a threaded core body. Claim 1 differs by the over-travel in which a surface moved by the poppet deforms an element to open a second flow path. The effect relied on, at [0010] and [0013], is that air through the purge gap removes sealant film from the surfaces it sweeps. The inspection at [0287] found cured film on exactly those surfaces after forty cycles. The surfaces found clean, the sealing edge and the sealing face, bound the main passage, where by [0011] the ordinary stream of air already flows. The comparison cannot attribute the longer life to the purge gap either: the conventional valve cores are unidentified ([0282]), their crack pressure, seat material and seat geometry are not given, and [0289] concedes that the two cleaning actions were never separated. With no effect shown for the distinguishing feature, the problem falls to providing a second flow path that opens at a higher pressure differential. Staged opening by further poppet travel is acknowledged at [0008] and shown in US4044791A; a ring that deforms radially outward to open a gap and returns when the valve closes is acknowledged at [0009] and shown in US5924444A, a valve for mounting on a tyre valve stem; cleaning a valve seat with air through an annular slit is in US3570510A. No embedded reference deforms the ring by a surface moved by the poppet; the examiner will call that a mechanical alternative to deformation by flow. The objection is credible against claims 1, 2 and 3 and against claims 38 and 57, which recite the air purge itself.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add what the inventor actually recorded: the state of the same surfaces on the conventional valve cores at failure, the identity and crack pressure of those valve cores, and any observation that air passed through the purge gap. If the inventor confirms it, restate [0010] and [0013] so that the effect asserted is the one the inspection supports, namely that the surfaces on which the poppet seals stay free of sealant film. Add, without touching claim 1, an independent fallback to the tested combination (claim 1 with claims 20 and 27), so that one claim rests on the example as run. No narrowing of claim 1 is proposed.

findings.title: Claim 3 claims the seat ring alone and is limited only by an intended use
findings.attack: The structure claimed is a tube, an edge at one end, a wall that is not straight, and elasticity. The poppet, the load-applying surface, the normal stroke, the over-travel, the main passage and the purge gap all belong to a valve core that claim 3 does not claim; they state what the ring is for and limit it only to suitability. The examiner reads the claim on any resilient tubular element of suitable size whose wall is not straight. The description itself equates the load-converting geometry with a zig-zag or diamond-cell pattern laser-cut in NiTi tube ([0171]); a tubular resilient metal seat engaged by a poppet, with undulating portions, is in US11549591B1, which [0166] acknowledges. No single embedded reference shows every feature, so the objection is put on common general knowledge (A3) for novelty and, failing that, on inventive step, together with a clarity objection that the ring is defined by parts it does not contain. If claim 3 falls, claims 4 and 78 to 83 add only the ordinary process chain for NiTi tube (US9126251B2) and claims 70 to 75 add known materials.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Breadth is kept where it is defensible: claim 1 and claim 77 claim the ring in its valve core. For the ring alone, narrowing appears to be the only credible route, and the human should decide it: recite structure that a known tube would not have for another reason, for example the fit band and the free portion of claim 66 with a continuous sealing edge. Scope given up: a loose ring without those features, which would then be reached only through claim 77 and indirect infringement.

findings.title: The axial and face-gap forms are described, stated not to be a radial expansion, and claimed nowhere
findings.attack: [0179] teaches a working alternative: a disc spring whose rim seals on a face, flattened by the load-applying surface in over-travel so that a purge gap opens at the face. The description then says in terms that this is not a radial expansion. Every independent claim requires a radial expansion of a radially deflectable element. A competitor builds [0179]: a catalogue disc spring, no NiTi, no shape-setting, and by [0179] the same part supplies the second spring stage. The product sells on the same promise, a second flow path opened by over-travel. Subject matter described and left unclaimed is open to the argument that it was given to the public, and an equivalents case has to overcome the applicant's own sentence.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add an independent claim, or broaden claim 1 and move radial expansion to a dependent claim, to a deflectable element whose deflection by the load-applying surface in the over-travel opens the purge gap, on the basis of [0179] and [0180]. Add a figure for the disc-spring form, since none exists, and conform [0014]. Nothing is narrowed.

findings.title: Every independent claim requires a contact-free first range of travel
findings.attack: Claims 1 and 2 require a normal stroke in which the surface is spaced from the element and the purge gap is closed; claim 3 requires an over-travel beyond a normal stroke. A competitor lets the load-applying surface rest on the deflectable element when the valve is closed, so that the element deflects and the second flow path opens progressively from the first movement of the poppet. There is then no normal stroke as defined in [0071] and no literal infringement of any claim. It works commercially: a single-rate spring, no threshold to tune, and a purge on every inflation whatever the pump delivers. With a rigid seat and a separate ring the seal is unaffected. [0015] and [0072] make the two ranges essential in the applicant's own words, which blocks equivalents and blocks later broadening. This is a negative limitation on internal behaviour in an independent claim.
findings.least_narrowing_action: If it is within the inventor's conception, add an embodiment in which the load-applying surface bears on the deflectable element from the start of the lift, and an independent claim without the spaced-throughout and closed-throughout limitations; keep those limitations as a dependent claim; recast [0015] as embodiment language. If it is not within the conception, this stays as a residual risk for the human.

findings.title: The definitions of seat ring and purge shoulder contradict claims 3, 15 with 20, 43 and 77
findings.attack: [0050] applies the definitions to the claims. A seat ring is defined as loaded by the purge shoulder and as retained in the core body, and the purge shoulder is defined as a surface of the poppet. Claims 20 to 32 depend through claim 15, where the load comes from a separate collar. Claim 43 claims a tapered seat ring loaded by a taper that [0178] says replaces the purge shoulder. Claim 3 claims a ring not yet in any core body, and [0162] says it is supplied loose. On the applicant's own lexicon none of these is a seat ring. The examiner objects that the claims and the description disagree. A defendant whose ring is loaded by a collar or a washer, or who sells loose rings, argues that it has no seat ring as the patent defines one.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Amend [0058] to refer to the load-applying surface, with the purge shoulder as the preferred example, and to a ring 'retained, in use, in the core body'. [0063] can stay. The row for seat ring in the locked terminology carries the same purge-shoulder wording and should be corrected by its owner. No claim changes and nothing is narrowed.

findings.title: The Background attributes a valve core to a publication number that belongs to an antenna application
findings.attack: The prior-art index records the document supplied under this number as fictional and not fetched. The public record for US20190123456A1 is 'Multiple-input multiple-output (mimo) omnidirectional antenna', Alpha Wireless Ltd (https://patents.google.com/patent/US20190123456A1/en, accessed 2026-09-29). As drafted, the Background cites a document that does not say what is attributed to it, and admits as prior art an enlarged bore, a fluoropolymer-coated sealing face, a rigid seat and a removable insert for sealant deposits. 'In the documents referred to above' in [0013] sweeps it in. An examiner may hold the applicant to the admission; an opponent will.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete [0007] and check that no other passage relies on it. Put nothing in its place unless a real document with saved text is identified.

findings.title: 'Closed at rest' is defined so that an open clearance counts as closed
findings.attack: By [0067] the purge gap is closed whenever its surfaces are in their unloaded position, and FIG. 4A is to be drawn with a clearance at rest. Opening the purge gap then cannot be told from widening a clearance that is already there. The edge of the claim is uncertain, and the claim moves towards art in which the deformation of a ring increases a gap (US5924444A). A defendant argues either that the claim is indefinite or that its permanently open clearance is never closed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add to [0067] a positive test that the inventor can confirm for the prototype, for example that at rest the purge gap offers no flow path from the upstream side to the tyre chamber; keep the sentence on gas-tightness. Correct the FIG. 4A instruction or explain the clearance. No claim changes.

findings.title: Snap-back wipe: the ring recovers while the sealing face is a full normal stroke away
findings.attack: By [0137] the ring recovers when the purge shoulder lifts, and only then does the poppet return through the normal stroke, which was 0.6 mm in the prototype ([0235]). At the moment of recovery the sealing face is not touching the ring. How the ring moves across that face and shears film from it is not disclosed; [0138] offers a belief. Claims 32, 56 and 76 recite it as fact.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the inventor's account of which surfaces touch during the recovery and when. If there is none, recast claims 32, 56 and 76 to what is disclosed: the ring recovers its shape at the sealing edge before the sealing face seats again.

findings.title: Categorical statements exclude any opening by pressure or flow
findings.attack: The description defines the invention against a flow path opened by pressure or flow. A competitor fits a resilient ring or sleeve that the pressure differential itself expands above a threshold: no load-applying surface, no purge shoulder, no two-rate spring, and the same second flow path at high pump pressure. It does not infringe literally, and the applicant's own sentences answer an equivalents case. These statements are also what separates claim 1 from US5924444A, so they cannot simply be removed.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Keep claim 1. Recast [0016] and [0135] as statements about the embodiments described, and confine [0013] to what each document says. If the inventor has conceived an opening assisted by pressure in addition to the mechanical load, add it as an embodiment.

findings.title: [0106] ties the functional terms to the structures described
findings.attack: 'Radially deflectable element', 'load-applying surface', 'return bias' and 'load-converting geometry' carry little structure of their own. [0106] says they cover each structure described. That is the scope a means-plus-function construction would give in the US, and in any forum it invites the argument that a structure not described is outside the term.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Reword [0106] to 'covers any structure that performs the function, including each structure described herein'. No claim changes.

findings.title: The actuating condition and the claimed values cannot be reproduced or checked from the text
findings.attack: The over-travel differential is a pressure difference across a poppet that is already open, so it depends on the flow delivered, which was not recorded. That the poppet reached the over-travel, and that the gap opened to 0.15 mm, rests on a sound heard when the pump head was removed. No method is given for measuring the crack pressure, the over-travel differential, the purge gap width inside an assembled valve core, or the austenite finish temperature, which is a supplier's specification. Claims 11, 12, 19, 29, 33, 34, 53 and 72 recite these values. A third party cannot tell whether it is inside them and the proprietor cannot prove that anyone is.
findings.least_narrowing_action: State how each value was measured or set in the prototype, and the method for the austenite finish temperature. Where a value is a design value and not a measurement, say so.

findings.title: FIG. 5 places both thresholds at the wrong end of their ranges
findings.attack: The figure marks the crack pressure at the end of the normal stroke and the over-travel differential at the end of the over-travel. [0069] and [0070] put each at the start of its range. A curve drawn from the origin shows no preload, so nothing holds the poppet closed until a crack pressure is reached. The drawing contradicts the definitions on which claims 5, 6 and 11 rest.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Correct the figure instruction: the curve starts at zero travel at the force that corresponds to the crack pressure, and the over-travel differential is marked at the change of slope.

findings.title: The fallback ladder adds conventional features and untested ranges
findings.attack: If claim 1 falls, most fallbacks do not rescue it. Claims 5 to 10 add return springs of ordinary two-stage kinds (A2). Claims 11, 12, 19, 33, 34, 68 and 69 add ranges for which [0230] disclaims any tested effect, so the examiner treats them as arbitrary. Claims 27 to 29 and 70 to 73 add a superelastic NiTi seat, a seat material already used in valves (US6019118A). Claims 35 to 37 add two materials and a lock nut that the description calls conventional. Claims 4 and 78 to 83 add the usual route for NiTi tube. The claims with structure peculiar to the invention are 20 to 26 and 40 to 44, and those are the untested forms.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete nothing. For each fallback that matters, state in the description the technical reason that ties the feature to the opening of the purge gap; some exist already at [0149] and [0188]. Add a mid-level independent fallback that combines claim 1 with claims 20, 21 and 25.

findings.title: One species built; the polymer, spring-metal and other forms are claimed on expectation
findings.attack: One form has been built. Claims 30, 31, 74 and 75 claim a PEEK ring of the prototype geometry although the description cannot say that such a ring would open the purge gap at all. The genus of claim 1 runs from a polymer to spring steel. In the US the question is whether the inventor had possession of the genus; at the EPO and in the UK it is whether the claim can be worked across its width without research. The candour of the text is to the applicant's credit, and each candid sentence is also an admission.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Add the design reasoning the inventor has, for example the strain in PEEK at the stated convolution amplitude and why the bending-dominated forms stay elastic. Keep the statements of what was not tested. Nothing is narrowed.

findings.title: The thermal variant uses 'purge gap' against its own definition, and unclaimed numbered statements remain
findings.attack: A purge gap as defined is opened in the over-travel by the load-applying surface. The thermal variant opens 'the purge gap' by warming, with the poppet seated. A defined term is used against its definition. The thermal variant, Statement 7.1 (a wiper ring with no purge gap), Statement 5.6 and Statements 2.5 and 2.6 fall outside every claim: the EPO will require the description brought into line, and in the US what is described and unclaimed is exposed. The numbered statements at [0297] to [0348] read as claims inside the description, which the EPO objects to before grant.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Present the thermal variant as a separate aspect outside the first aspect and word [0065] 'in the first aspect'. Counsel decides whether to claim it separately or in a divisional. Recast the numbered statements as numbered embodiments in prose; do not delete them, because they are basis for amendment.

findings.title: Figures and registry carry a figure, numerals and status captions that the description does not
findings.attack: FIG. 13A and numeral 220 are in the figure set and the registry but not in the description, which lists FIG. 13B alone. Numerals 402 and 404 are called for on FIG. 5 and appear in neither the registry table nor the description. The captions for FIGS. 10 to 13 put statements of status on the drawing sheets. No figure shows the collar of claim 15, the springs of claims 9 and 10 or the valve stem bore of claim 45, and the US requires the drawings to show every claimed feature. The figure plan in the package records that the constructions of FIGS. 11, 12 and 13A were not in the inventor's disclosure and await confirmation, yet claims 26, 40 to 44 and 67 claim them. The figure files also carry process notes, such as references to the inventor's sketch files and to claim strategy, which are not filing text and which a blind package should not contain.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Describe FIG. 13A and numeral 220 in the description or remove both, renumbering FIG. 13B if FIG. 13A goes. Register 402 and 404 or drop them. Take the status captions off the drawings; the description already says what was built. Add figures for the claimed collar, spring constructions and valve stem bore. Strip the process notes. Whether the constructions of claims 26, 40 to 44 and 67 are confirmed as the inventor's is for the human (Q2).

findings.title: Four categories and two valve cores of different scope
findings.attack: The set claims a valve core, a method of use, a seat ring and a method of making it, and a second valve core in claim 77 that recites no load-applying surface. If claim 3 is not new (F-32-4), the seat ring group, claims 3, 4 and 62 to 86, shares no special technical feature with the valve core group. A US restriction between the four groups is to be expected. Claim 77 introduces 'a valve core' and 'a poppet' that claim 3 has already introduced, so it is unclear whether they are the same parts.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Delete nothing. Plan for a divisional on the seat ring and its manufacture. In claim 77 say that the poppet is the poppet whose sealing face seats on the sealing edge of the seat ring.

findings.title: Multiple dependencies, a colliding term in claim 42, and claims limited by things outside the claimed product
findings.attack: Forty-five of the 86 claims are multiple dependent, and 37 of those depend on another multiple dependent claim, from claim 13 onward. The US does not accept that form, and counted the US way the set runs to several hundred claims. 'Split seat' is a locked synonym of the two-piece seat, so 'split seat ring' in claim 42 and [0177] can be read as the two-piece seat; `pc terms` flags it on the claims. Claim 50 limits a tyre valve by a tyre chamber and by sealant, neither of which is part of the valve claimed, and claim 38 defines the valve core by an air flow and a sealant film that exist only in use.
findings.least_narrowing_action: Prepare a US claim set with single dependencies on the chains that matter. Declare 'split seat ring' as a new term, or rename it, and take 'split seat' out of the synonyms of the two-piece seat. Recast claim 50 as a tyre chamber fitted with the tyre valve and containing sealant, for which Statement 2.5 at [0327] is basis.

assumptions.text: The package is the whole of the text to be filed. The figure plan and the figure instructions are instructions to the draftsperson; the captions they prescribe would appear on the drawings.
Common general knowledge: return springs with two stages, by variable pitch, by springs in series or nested, or by a stop engaging a second spring, are ordinary machine elements.
Common general knowledge: thin-walled resilient tubes with a convoluted or patterned wall, such as small bellows and laser-cut tubes, change diameter under axial load and recover when it is removed.

Prior art is limited to the references saved under prior-art/refs and listed in the index. Every passage quoted from them, and every passage quoted from the package, was checked by script against the saved text. The public record of US20190123456A1 was fetched by publication number only.
Statutory provisions and office practice are named from general knowledge as issues for counsel. No case law is relied on and nothing here is a legal conclusion.
This review is an analysis aid produced by AI. It clears nothing for filing; qualified patent counsel reviews and signs off.

open_questions.text: For the inventor: in the tested valve cores, where does the purge shoulder bear on the seat ring, what reacts the load, where does air enter the purge gap, and which contact closes it at rest?

For the human: have the constructions of FIGS. 11, 12 and 13A, claimed in claims 26, 40 to 44 and 67, been confirmed as the inventor's own? The package says they await confirmation. Inventorship cannot be assessed from the package.
For the inventor: what does the laboratory record show for the dates, the hold period and the cycle counts of Example 1?
For the inventor: were the surfaces of the conventional valve cores inspected at failure, and what were those valve cores?
For the inventor: has an arrangement been conceived in which the element is deflected from the start of the lift, or in which pressure assists the opening?
For counsel: has any prototype been shown or used outside confidence since August 2026? Cannot be answered from the package.
